summary: After Dow -800/Nasdaq -4%, SGX broke 16,900 - a 500-pt round trip from Friday's 17,400. China PMI below 50 again; GST collections record 1.68 lakh cr; Tata Motors sales +75%. LIC IPO anchor book watched; HDFC twins and IndusInd results due; range 16,800-17,400.

LIC IPO anchor book opened May 2; issue to open May 4; priced 900-950

India manufacturing PMI printed 54-55, indicating expansion

LIC subscription watched hourly; HDFC twins stabilized by DII NAV support; Infosys ADR green; Kotak results due (speaker holds 1800 straddle); OI shows 17,300 resistance after ignoring margin-driven 17,500 OI.

Fed widely expected to hike 50bp at May 2022 meeting - a pre-announced, expected move
Reliance Q4 results due May 6; market speculated record profit and Jio/retail demerger plans

lessons: Markets react violently to unexpected news, not expected news - pre-announced events should not scare you.
In volatile times watch the VIX, not the price: falling VIX ahead of an event signals calm, not complacency.

summary: Unscheduled RBI announcement at 2pm: repo +40bp and CRR +50bp shocked markets - Nifty fell ~500 pts high-to-low, broke 16,800 decisively; next support seen at 15,700. FIIs sold 3,300 cr, DIIs 1,300 cr; LIC IPO policyholder portion full but FIIs absent. Speaker exits longs, sells calls.

events.claim: RBI unexpectedly raised repo rate by 40bp to 4.4% and CRR by 50bp in an unscheduled announcement on May 4, 2022
Bank Nifty fell ~400-500 points after the CRR hike news
LIC IPO policyholder portion fully subscribed; FIIs largely absent from anchor/subscription
Kotak Mahindra Bank results came in good intraday

lessons: Markets react violently to shocks: RBI hiked less than the Fed's 50bp but crashed Indian markets because it was unscheduled.
Hope is the worst enemy in the stock market - decisive broken support means exit, not hope.
A CRR hike can hurt banks more than a repo hike because CRR deposits earn no interest.
quote: Hope is the worst enemy in the stock market.

summary: Fed delivered the expected 50bp; Powell's presser sent Dow +1,000 in an hour back above 34,000. Contrast: India's smaller 40bp unscheduled hike crashed the market. CRR mechanics explained (4%→4.5%, interest-free); Bank Nifty -400-500 on CRR news. SGX ~16,850; 16,500 max put OI; bearish Bank Nifty bias.

events.claim: US Fed raised rates 50bp on May 4, 2022 as expected; Dow rallied over 1,000 points within about an hour after the Powell presser
Dow had broken 34,000 then regained it after the Fed
RBI raised CRR from 4% to 4.5% effective (May 2022), interest-free for banks

lessons: Expected bad news is already priced; surprise - even smaller in magnitude - is what crashes markets.
When a strong support breaks with momentum, it flips to resistance (16,800 → resistance).

summary: Short covering took Nifty to ~16,980, then -300: 'amateurs open, professionals close'. Dow's +1,000 couldn't move India +10. FIIs sold 2,100 cr; 11,000 cr in 4 sessions signals 40k cr month. India VIX fell ~10% intraday. LIC IPO fully subscribed with almost no FII participation. Reliance -40 Nifty pts pre-results.

events.claim: FIIs sold ~11,000 cr in the first four sessions of the May 2022 series, on pace for ~40,000 cr for the month
LIC IPO became fully subscribed without meaningful FII participation (one FII bid for 225 shares)
India VIX fell about 10% intraday despite market weakness

lessons: A 1,000-point Dow rally moving Nifty by ten points is a verdict: local sellers, not global weakness, drive the tape.
Stocks that run up hard into results get profit-booked; stocks beaten down get short-covered - position accordingly.
quote: Amateurs open the market and professionals close the market.

summary: Dow -1,000+, Nasdaq -5% (worst since COVID); Netflix -70%, Meta -50%, Amazon -30-35% from highs. FIIs 75% short in index futures; 16,500 monthly max-OI already tested in week one. Netflix down ~70%, Meta ~50%, Amazon ~30-35% from their highs (as of May 2022)
FII index-futures positions were ~75% short in early May 2022
India F&O turnover is ~100x cash market turnover, ~90x of it in options

lessons: In a huge gap down, expect a reversal toward the previous close ~80% of the time - the bigger the gap, the bigger the snap-back.
When consensus shorts build to extremes, the setup is contrarian-bullish even while the tape bleeds.

FIIs sold 5,500 cr on May 6, taking May-2022 selling past 15,000 cr in five sessions
Hong Kong and China markets fell 3-4% on COVID statement

lessons: Currency follows equity outflows: when FIIs repatriate rather than redeploy, the rupee falls and fear compounds.

summary: Dow futures -400; Nasdaq -25%+ and falling. Nifty cut from 17,400 (Apr 29) toward 16,200 = ~1,200 pts in 5-6 sessions. FIIs 78% short - worse than COVID. Axis Mutual Fund front-running scandal broke in May 2022, triggering redemption fears

Nifty fell ~1,200 points (17,400→~16,200) in 5-6 sessions from April 29 to May 9, 2022

lessons: Small unnoticed news (a fund-scam tweet) can be the tip of an iceberg - connect scattered signals before they become the story.

quote: Sometimes you see a small news... later you understand that is just a tip of the iceberg.

summary: Tested 16,153, snapped +250, then chopped all day - FII selling vs DII buying both ~3,000+ cr. Four of seven heavyweights (Infosys, TCS, HDFC twins) green; Reliance alone -90 of Nifty's 110 pts. 16,500 huge OI = resistance; speaker runs 16,200 straddle (~300 premium). FII holding of Nifty-500 down 21%→18.5%. No bottom-fishing.

Reliance fell ~4% post-results, contributing ~90 of Nifty's 110-point fall on May 9, 2022
US CPI data due Wednesday May 11, 2022

lessons: Headline index moves can hide the real story: check which one heavyweight manufactured the fall.

summary: Dow collapsed 400 pts in the last half hour - institutional selling; Nasdaq -27% from high with 10% in three days = capitulation. events.claim: Dow fell ~400 points in the final half hour overnight (May 9-10, 2022), from -350 to nearly -750
Nasdaq down 27% from its high with 10% of that in three sessions; top 5-6 IT companies lost ~$1 trillion market cap in three days

Capitulation - when the bluest chips collapse - historically marks proximity to a low.

summary: Apple -5% again (~-$250bn cumulative, below Saudi Aramco as world's most valuable) = blue-chip capitulation; India has fallen >30% only 3x in 20 years (Lehman, COVID, 2004). lessons: When the bluest blue chips capitulate, the market is usually near a low - the remaining fall tends to be limited.

quote: Capitulation means surrender - and when bluest blue chips surrender, the market should be somewhere near the low.

lessons: Panic in one asset class (crypto) leaks into equities through margin calls - watch correlated leverage, not just news.

summary: Gap-up +160 used by FIIs to sell: 2pm free fall took Nifty -400 and Bank Nifty -1,000 intraday. SBI results okay yet stock fell 8% with futures at a 5-rupee discount - consensus shorting. FIIs 3,800 cr vs DIIs 3,200 cr; the real problem is absent buyers, not seller size. New weekly series opened with heavy 16,000+ call writing.

events.claim: Bank Nifty fell ~1,000 points intraday on May 13, 2022; SBI fell ~8% from intraday high despite okay results

lessons: Stable markets attract buyers; in chaos there are no buyers - so modest net selling produces outsized falls.
When every rise is sold into, accept the new normal: reduce size, shorten horizon, respect intraday reversals.
quote: It is a lack of buying rather than selling that is bringing the market to crazy levels.

SBI fell 7-8% from intraday high on May 13 despite good results

lessons: Markets price lead indicators (lockdown easing), not lag indicators (last month's production data).
When fundamentals (good results) stop moving stocks, positioning - the sellers' overhang - is the only truth.
quote: If I have to explain the market in one word: fragile.

Bank Nifty resistance seen at 34,000; Nifty at 16,000

lessons: When DIIs and FIIs each defend a level, the space between becomes the tradable range until one side breaks.
Late-session futures premium turning positive is an early tell that shorts are covering.

Paytm, the second-largest Indian IPO, traded ~70% below its 2,150 issue (~600) before bouncing ~10%

lessons: A Doji after a waterfall decline marks equilibrium: size down and wait for the market to declare direction.
Government-company listings (Coal India, LIC) reward dividend patience, not listing-gain speculation.

Target fell 22% and Walmart ~12% on weak results (week of May 18, 2022), hammering US retail
